answer: node2vec is not really training a standard supervised single hidden-layer feedforward neural network; it learns node embeddings by maximizing a skip-gram-style objective over random walks, and in common implementations the parameters are updated with Adam because it is a practical optimizer for this kind of sparse, noisy embedding objective. Adam uses adaptive per-parameter learning rates and momentum estimates, which often makes optimization faster and more stable than plain stochastic gradient descent, especially when the objective is nonconvex and the gradients are sparse. So the reason is mainly optimization convenience and performance, not because the model architecture requires Adam instead of SGD.
confidence_reasoning: This is a well-established description of node2vec and Adam, though exact optimizer choice can vary by implementation rather than being intrinsic to the algorithm.
